title: Senior Noncommissioned Logistician
raw_text:
10-92Z. MOS 92Z--Senior Noncommissioned Logistician, CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
    a. Major duties. The senior noncommissioned logistician supervises Soldiers engaged in supply and services,
materiel, petroleum, fatality and culinary management, aerial delivery operations, shower and laundry, water
treatment and logistics operations. They performed these duties in a multifunctional logistics environment. Duties
for MOS 92Z at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 92Z5O. The Senior Noncommissioned Logistician Master Sergeant (MSG) (MOS 92A, 92F, 92W
and 92Y) shape and execute comprehensive logistical strategies at the brigade or higher echelon level, directly
impacting mission success. Develop and refine logistical doctrine, policies, and procedures, influencing Army-
wide standards. Advise commanders and staff on all facets of logistics, including supply, maintenance,
transportation, water management, and financial resource allocation. Direct the synchronization of logistical
efforts across multiple units and organizations, ensuring seamless support. Manage and oversee substantial
budgets, optimizing resource utilization and maximizing return on investment. Mentor and develop subordinate
logistical leaders, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and professional excellence. Represent the
command in high-level logistical forums, collaborating with interagency partners and allied forces. Anticipate
future logistical challenges, proactively developing innovative solutions and mitigating potential risks. Conduct
strategic assessments of logistical capabilities, identifying areas for enhancement and modernization. Champion
the integration of emerging technologies and best practices to optimize logistical efficiency and effectiveness.
       (2) MOSC 92Z6O. The Senior Noncommissioned Logistician Sergeant Major (SGM) (MOSs 92Z5O,
92G5O, 92M5O, 92R5P, and 92S5O) envisions and implements the overarching logistical strategy for a division,
corps, or theater-level command, directly enabling sustained operations. Advise the commanding general,
directors and staff on all logistical matters, provide critical insights and recommendations. Direct and synchronize
the efforts of multiple logistical brigades and battalions, ensuring seamless support across a vast area of
responsibility. Develop and enforce logistical policies, standards, and procedures, maintain accountability and
maximizing efficiency. Manage budget and allocate resources strategically to meet evolving operational needs.
Mentor and develop logistical leaders, fostering a culture of excellence and preparing them for future
opportunities. Represent the command at the highest levels, collaborating with interagency partners, allied
nations, and civilian authorities. Anticipate and mitigate logistical risks, proactively addressing potential
disruptions to supply chains and support networks. Employ innovation and the adoption of cutting-edge
technologies to transform logistical capabilities. Serve as the principal logistical authority, shaping the future of
Army logistics and ensuring readiness for any contingency.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Senior Noncommissioned Logisticians,
MOS 92Z, must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Physical profile of 222232.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) A minimum score in aptitude area—N/A.
         (5) This MOS is closed for reclassification into the MOS except for the normal career progression of
Soldiers in the 92 CMF MOSs through promotion.
    c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all MOS)).
         (1) 3C--Operation Contract Support (OCS) (SSG and above).
         (2) 8R--Master Resilience Trainer (MRT).
         (3) 3D--Level II Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Industrial/Contract Property
Management Certification.
        (4) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only).
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are
listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92Z-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-92Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
